test(daemon): a handoff over a moving bar can move, and comments say what a feed answers (candybar-isolated-daemon-bfab.dnr)

Answers the plan review of #553. A reader's `encoding: "frame"` request on a
followed session is the request the feed draws by, and nothing on the feed path
reads `encoding`, so three comments claiming a feed frame is that request's
answer go. The handoff's stand-in was shown only on a still bar, where a literal
`still` reads the same, so a case runs it over a moving one. The encoding e2e
now asserts backgrounds and attributes crossed the wire, and that depth `none`
carries neither.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(daemon): a one-shot reader asks for the Frame, scripts and site decode nothing (candybar-isolated-daemon-bfab.dnr)

With decoding ruled out, a script or harness holding one render's answer had
no other way to read the bar. A render request can now state `encoding`, `ansi`
or `frame`. Absent is `ansi`, and the shipped clients never send it, so
`RenderRequest` stays what they send, key for key, and the protocol check needs
no exemption; `ReaderRenderRequest` adds the field. A bad value is refused at
the checkpoint, and `encoding` lands on the render event.

The answer is encoded inside the draw's turn, so `drew`, which DRAW_RESERVE_MS
is held to, still times the bytes. `statuslineOf` returns a Frame, and the
handoff line and the diagnostics viewer share one stand-in, since both draw
still text over a bar that can move again.

`linksOf` replaces `links` and `drawnLinks` in src/click/read.ts, and
site/transport.ts, scripts/bar-web/server.ts, scripts/drive-bar.ts and the bench
link lookup read Frames. Bench ticks stay on the client's own request. src holds
no reader of rendered bytes now: src/render/ansi.ts goes, and the byte readers
tests still use move to test/helpers/ansi.ts until the epic's last ticket.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(render): band and tmux encode Frames, nothing in src decodes ANSI (candybar-isolated-daemon-bfab.2nq) (#552)

* refactor(render): band and tmux encode Frames, nothing in src decodes ANSI (candybar-isolated-daemon-bfab.2nq)

The band and tmux status lanes read the drawn Frame instead of decoding the
bytes the render wrote. Every FeedFrame has a bar: a failed render's is the
diagnostic Frame, in the words of the statusline's error glyph, so a lane
holds no failure branch and planOutcome leaves every surface the daemon draws.

Sink carries the bar beside the lane's JSON, and feed.last holds it once per
push for a late joiner. mergedRuns joins neighbouring runs of one look, as the
decoder did, so one tmux link stays one range. laneEncoded is the one refusal
point, replacing both catch arms. nextChange and motion leave FeedFrame and
drawRender's return, because the Frame states them.

* refactor(render): one drawn colour has one spelling, and a lane refuses inside its encoder (candybar-isolated-daemon-bfab.2nq)

Answers the high review of #552.

- A Run spells a terminal colour `color(n)` whichever name drew it, so a
  hex downgraded beside `red` is one look. mergedRuns then does what it
  says at every depth: the spelled-look exception is gone, and ANSI bytes
  and the lane snapshots do not move.
- bandFrame and tmuxStatusFrame are total: laneEncoded lives inside each,
  so a caller cannot reach the throw and a follower's push cannot abort.
- The feed's answer is `resp`, because `answers.bar` read as the Frame
  beside `feed.last.bar`.
- Lanes map a Run's attrs directly. Run.attrs already holds what is on.
- A Run's link is clean only because RichText admitted it, and band and
  tmux write it past rich-js's encoder, so that is stated and tested.

gitaculous already shows the location, so the default layout drops directory

The default identity row and five bundled presets (compact, verbose, zen,
git, dense) still placed `directory` beside `gitaculous`, which now draws
the checkout path itself. Every default user saw the path twice. The
directory segment stays defined in the library; only its placement goes.

Tests that read the bundled layout now name a segment the bar still places,
and the doc fence shows the one path it renders.

Known consequence: `zen` now holds only `context`, so it no longer shows
where you are. Its comment still describes the old intent.
